summary: Jim Rheingans works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at Hamburg and a PhD through the University of the West of England and Bath Spa University under David P. Jackson, Mahinda Deegalle, and Fiona Montgomery, later holding attested posts at Hamburg, Vienna, and Sydney.

Jin Kemu (1912–2000) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Sinology. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University (1941–1945) and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Peking University beginning in 1948.

Jin Kyoung Choi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. Choi studied at the University of Munich and Ghent University, later holding posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and as a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University.

Jin Y. Park works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Park served as Assistant Professor of Philosophy and Religion at American University (attested 2007–2012) and was a visiting fellow at City University of Hong Kong.

Jinah Kim works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She completed her PhD at UC Berkeley under Joanna Gottfried Williams. Kim held posts at Vanderbilt and the Institute for Advanced Study, becoming Professor of Indian and South Asian Art at Harvard.
Jinchuan Wan specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy, holding posts as a professor at both National Central University and Fo Guang University (attested 2010).
Jing Yin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti. He served as Director at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2006–2010).

Jing-shen Tao (born 1933) is a historian and Sinologist. After studying at National Taiwan University and earning his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington, he served as Professor of East Asian Studies at the University of Arizona (~1976–2000) and at Academia Sinica.
Jingyi Yang works in Indology, Tibetology, and computational fields. Yang studied at the University of Hamburg and held a post there as a research project employee (attested 2026).

Jinhua Chen works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at McMaster University and completed postdoctoral research at Kyoto University under Noritoshi Aramaki. He held positions at the University of Virginia and as professor of East Asian Buddhism at the University of British Columbia.

Jinhua Jia specializes in Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After earning a PhD at the University of Colorado Boulder under Paul W. Kroll, Jia held posts at Colorado, Harvard, the Institute for Advanced Study, and The Hong Kong Polytechnic University.
Jinling He is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Hiroki Okumura.
Jinping Liao is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.

Jinshi Fan (born 1938) is a specialist in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University under Bai Su (~1958–1963) and served as Director of the Dunhuang Academy (1984–2014), later holding a post at Lanzhou University.

Jinzhang Peng (1937–2017) was a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held a post at Wuhan University (~1963–1986) before serving as a researcher and professor at the Dunhuang Academy (~1986–2017).

Jiro Abe (1883–1959) worked in philosophy and Japanology. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1904–1907), he held posts at Japan Women's University (~1913–1923) and Tohoku University (~1923–1945).

Jiro Kawakita (1920–2009) was a scholar in Tibetology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1939–1943) and held posts at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1960–1977), the University of Tsukuba (~1977–1984), and Chubu University (~1985–1992).

Jiro Murata (1895–1985) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1917–1920) and later held a post at the National Institute of Technology, Akashi College (~1962–1967).

Jiro Sugiyama (1928–2011) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Tokyo National Museum (~1957–1989), Nagaoka University of Technology (~1989–1994), Bukkyo University, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.
Jiryo Masuda worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied under Unrai Wogihara. He later served as a professor at the University of Calcutta.
